title: Quizzy.News
summary: A daily news trivia game I designed and launched to help teens and adults keep up with current events from reputable sources.
intro: Quizzy.News is a short daily quiz on national and global news from the last 24 hours, made for people who love a quick game like Wordle. I took it from concept to launch: research, design, testing, and leading a volunteer team of developers to build it.
body:
## Why I built it

As a teacher, I watched students arrive each morning repeating misinformation from social media. According to the American Psychological Association, fewer than 20% of US teens read a book, magazine or newspaper daily for pleasure, while more than 80% use social media every day. Quizzy.News is my answer: a fun, quick way to stay up to date from reputable sources.

## Testing the game

I interviewed people of different ages and news habits. Most cared about the news but worried about which sources to trust, and said they’d keep up more if it were fun. I then ran a moderated usability study with five participants on a low-fidelity prototype, testing the flow, the 60-second timer, question length and the number of answers.

![Low fidelity prototype](/images/quizzynews/lo-fi-prototype-3.gif)
![Low fidelity prototype](/images/quizzynews/lo-fi-prototype-2.gif)

*The low-fidelity prototype.*

## What changed

Three findings shaped the final design: clearer wording, with details like dates in view; a score that’s always visible; and more to do at the end, like reading further and sharing results.

![Before usability study](/images/quizzynews/mockup-slide-1-a.png)
![After usability study](/images/quizzynews/mockup-slide-1-b.png)

*Question wording, before (left) and after (right) testing.*

![Before usability study](/images/quizzynews/mockup-slide-2-a.png)
![After usability study](/images/quizzynews/mockup-slide-2-b.png)

*The score and results page, before (left) and after (right).*

![First high fidelity screens](/images/quizzynews/first-hi-fi-screens.png)

*High-fidelity screens.*

Color contrast works for people with low vision, and right and wrong answers are marked with icons as well as color.

![Responsive screens](/images/quizzynews/responsive-screens.png)

*Mobile, tablet and desktop.*

## Outcome

I took Quizzy.News from concept to launch, leading a volunteer team of three-plus developers. It’s live at [quizzy.news](https://www.quizzy.news).
